description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) in percentage as a function of the co-occurrence number for five different methods: Base, MEND, FT, IKE, and ROME. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," is on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 1000, with tick marks at 10^0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", is on a linear scale from 60 to 80, with major gridlines at 65, 70, 75, and 80. The "Base" method is represented by a black line with circular markers, starting at approximately 64% accuracy and increasing to about 71% as the co-occurrence number increases. The "MEND" method, shown with a brown line and diamond markers, starts at around 70.5% and rises to approximately 80%. The "FT" method, depicted with a blue line and triangle markers, begins at about 65.5% and increases to roughly 73%. The "IKE" method, represented by a red line with triangle markers, starts at approximately 67% and increases to about 75%. The "ROME" method, shown with a green line and square markers, starts at around 74% and increases to approximately 82%. All five methods show a general upward trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases.
